# Today {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## How the session runs

| | |
|---|---|
| **0–10** | What is being assessed, and what is not |
| **10–150** | Ten presentations, 12 minutes each |
| **150–170** | Cross-group questions |
| **170–180** | Close |

::: {.check}
Every member presents. Which member takes which part is **drawn at the start of
your slot**, not chosen by your group.
:::

## Why the draw exists

Not to catch anybody out.

::: {.tight}
- A group where one person understands the model has not learned the material
- The draw makes shared understanding the only viable strategy
- It is announced from Session 01, so nobody is surprised
:::

::: {.muted}
The group that prepares by teaching each other its own work is doing exactly
what the assessment is designed to produce.
:::

# The shape {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Twelve minutes

| Minutes | Content |
|---|---|
| **0–2** | The question, and why it is not trivial |
| **2–4** | The data, its coverage and its gaps |
| **4–7** | The method, and why this one |
| **7–10** | What you found, with uncertainty |
| **10–12** | What it does **not** license |

::: {.warn}
The last two minutes carry more marks than the middle three. Plan them first.
:::

## What earns marks

::: {.tight}
- A **precisely stated estimand** — prediction or effect, named in one sentence
- Validation that matches the claim — the right split, the right horizon
- Uncertainty presented as part of the result, not an apology after it
- A limitation you found yourselves, before anyone asked
- An answer of "we cannot claim that" where it is the correct answer
:::

## What loses them

::: {.tight}
- $R^2$ with no error in the units of the outcome
- Causal verbs on a predictive model — *drives*, *causes*, *leads to*
- A construct named as though it were a measurement
- A model with no statement of when it stops being valid
- Three members, one of whom has clearly not run the code
:::

::: {.warn}
"Our lasso selected these six variables and here are their p-values" will be
asked about, and there is no good answer.
:::

# The defence {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Questions you should expect

::: {.tight}
- *Why that cross-validation split, and what changes under a different one?*
- *Which coefficient moves most if your main confounder is real?*
- *What does your index correlate with that it should not?*
- *How many rows did you drop, and who were they?*
- *What is your retirement trigger, and where does it come from?*
:::

::: {.check}
All five are answerable from work you have already done — if you did it.
:::

## How to answer well

::: {.tight}
- **Say the number.** "About 12%" beats "quite a lot."
- **Say "I don't know"** when you don't. Then say how you would find out.
- **Do not defend a weak claim.** Concede it and state the stronger one you can support.
:::

::: {.muted}
Conceding a point accurately is evidence of understanding. Defending an
indefensible one is evidence of the opposite.
:::

## The three sentences

Every lab this term ended with three sentences. This is why.

> **What we estimated. How confident we are. What it does not license.**

::: {.check}
If your twelve minutes collapse to those three sentences and they are right, you
have done the course.
:::

# After {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## What to submit

::: {.tight}
- Slides, in the repository, before your slot
- The governance file from Session 11, complete
- A repository that runs from a clean clone
- Your role log, current
- Peer ratings, sent separately — see [`FORM.md`](../assessment/peer-ratings/FORM.md)
:::

::: {.warn}
"It runs on my machine" is not a submission. Clone your own repository into a
fresh folder and run it before you present.
:::

## What you should take away

::: {.tight}
- The methods are standard, and you can now read a paper that uses them
- The judgement is not standard, and it is the part that transfers
- Most of the skill is in **the sentence you refuse to write**
:::

::: {.muted}
You will forget the syntax. Keep the habit of asking what the number entitles
you to say.
:::
